_description: Batch 7 — post-launch expansion toward ~300 new bands, opening the jam-band scene and the classic/hard-rock canon. Same rule as every batch before it: nothing is admitted that does not connect to a band or musician already in the graph, and the operator-requested anchors below are the only entries that get credit for being asked for rather than for overlap they already have. Seeded against a fresh snapshot of the live Neon graph (scripts/data/live-graph-seed.csv, 499 bands / 2757 musicians) rather than the original Seattle CSV, so 'already in the graph' means what is actually in production tonight.
_mandatory_anchors: KISS, ZZ Top, Led Zeppelin, AC/DC, Journey and Supertramp were named by the operator and must appear in the results.
_bridge_strategy: The persons list is chosen for reach, not fame. Each one is a musician whose MusicBrainz member-of relations are expected to cross from the requested new territory into the graph as it already exists, so the additions arrive as connected neighbourhoods instead of islands. The deliberate bridges: John Paul Jones -> Them Crooked Vultures -> Dave Grohl, already in the graph, which is what ties Led Zeppelin in rather than parking it on its own. Gregg Rolie is the single node joining Santana and Journey. Ann and Nancy Wilson put Heart into a Seattle-rooted graph that already holds most of that city's personnel. Les Claypool and Stewart Copeland tie Oysterhead to Primus and The Police, which is the jam scene's cleanest route into alt-rock. Warren Haynes and Oteil Burbridge connect the Allman/Gov't Mule/Dead axis to itself in three directions. Bill Bruford spans Yes, King Crimson and Genesis in one person.
